advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make _revert_partial_fold mirror _rollback_fold's data-loss guard: track whether every reverse-rename succeeded and remove the snapshot only when the revert was clean, otherwise retain it as SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT for fsck.
evidence: compact_recovery.py:136-145: `if os.path.exists(retired) and not os.path.exists(original): try: os.rename(retired, original) except OSError: logger.warning(...)` then unconditionally `try: os.remove(snapshot)`
compact_txn.py:356-378: the in-process twin tracks `rollback_clean` and only removes `final_path` when `rollback_clean` is True, else retains the SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT state 'to avoid data loss'
compact_txn.py:300-322: _retire_folded_sources documents the same data-loss guard: removing the SNAPSHOT while a source is stuck retired is 'silent data loss'
ABSENCE: test_rollback_retains_snapshot_when_reverse_rename_fails exercises _txn._rollback_fold only; no test covers _revert_partial_fold with a failing reverse-rename
compact_recovery.py:120-125: `probe = _git(...cat-file -e...); if probe.returncode == 0: return True; if probe.returncode == 124: return None; return False`

compact_recovery.py:113-117 docstring: 'run_git_write(check=False) also fails non-zero on transient faults, and misreading one of those as "absent from HEAD" would revert a LANDED fold' — yet only rc-124 is treated as indeterminate
advisory.finding: _revert_partial_fold (recovery path) removes the uncommitted snapshot UNCONDITIONALLY even when a reverse-rename of a *.retired source failed, unlike its in-process twin _rollback_fold which retains the snapshot when any reverse-rename fails to avoid silent data loss. A source stranded as *.retired has its effect living only in the SNAPSHOT; deleting the SNAPSHOT during recovery then drops that event.
merged_from: _snapshot_in_head classifies any non-zero, non-124 return code from `git cat-file -e HEAD:<snapshot>` as a definite 'absent from HEAD' (False -> revert). After `rev-parse --verify HEAD` succeeds, a transient/non-124 fault on the cat-file probe (I/O error, object-db hiccup) is misread as absent and reverts a fold that actually landed.
scenarios: Recovery of an abandoned fold where restoring a *.retired source fails (e.g. permission/FS error) — the snapshot holding that source's folded event is then deleted, losing the event.
advisory.suggested_fix: Track a `revert_clean` flag over the reverse-rename loop (set False on OSError) and gate `os.remove(snapshot)` on it, retaining the snapshot and logging the fsck guidance otherwise, matching _rollback_fold.
